pages.hook: City buses in the USA can be a cheap way to travel, but each city has its own rules. Knowing how to ask a few questions makes your first ride easy.
pages.polite: Say **“Thank you”** to the driver when you get off. Many riders do it.

mythfact.s: In many US cities, bus drivers do not give change if you pay in cash.
mythfact.why: Many systems ask for exact fare, so keep coins or use a card.

mythfact.s: School buses in the USA are yellow.
mythfact.why: The yellow color is very well known.

mythfact.s: You shout the name of your stop to the driver.
mythfact.why: You press the stop button or pull the cord.

mythfact.s: Every American bus is free.
mythfact.why: Most city buses charge a fare, though some cities offer free routes.

decode.q: How do you ask the bus to stop?
decode.why: “Press the button to request a stop.”

compare.br: In Brazil, many people use a card at the turnstile (some lines still have a cobrador), and buses can get very full.
compare.us: In the USA you usually pay the driver at the front or tap a card, and you press the button to get off.
compare.tip: Keep your card or small bills ready before the bus arrives.
compare.ask: How do you pay for the bus in your city? Say it in English.

quiz.why: Fare = the price of the ride.

pages.title: Reading quest — Waiting for the bus in the city · part 1
text: This morning I waited at a bus stop in the city. A man named Ethan was next to me. He looked at the sign, then he looked at me. “**Excuse me, does this bus go downtown?**” he asked.
“**Yes, it goes downtown**,” I said. “**How much is the fare?**” he asked. “**Two dollars and fifty cents**,” I answered. “**Do I pay the driver?**” “**Yes, or use a card**.”
Then the bus came. It was blue and white, and it was almost empty. We got on, and Ethan put the money in the machine. “**How long does it take?**” he asked. “**About twenty minutes**,” I said.

opts: A short talk and a bus ride downtown
fast.why: Two people talk at a bus stop and ride downtown.

scan.q: How long does the trip take?

tf.s: The writer presses the stop button.

order: Ethan asks if the bus goes downtown.
The writer says the fare is $2.50.
They get on the bus.
The writer presses the stop button.
They say goodbye and get off.

ctx.sent: A simple talk made my morning better.

pages.think: Do you take the bus? Tell a friend how to pay and how to stop it.

pages.title: Reading quest — Waiting for the bus in the city · part 2
text: We sat near a window. The city moved past us: buildings, trees, people with coffee. I like buses because I can look outside and think. Ethan took a small notebook and wrote the name of each street.
When we came near downtown, I pressed the stop button. A red light said “Stop requested.” Ethan stood up and said, “**Enjoy your trip!**” I smiled and said, “You too!”
I thanked the driver and got off. A simple talk at a bus stop made my morning better.
